summary: Travis Air Force Base — one of the largest military airlift facilities on the West Coast — sits squarely within Fairfield's city limits, making the base not just a backdrop but a primary economic engine that shapes everything from housing demand to retail turnover. That military and logistics spine, combined with the Anheuser-Busch brewery and Jelly Belly factory also headquartered nearby, gives Fairfield more employment self-sufficiency than most Solano County cities, though a significant share of the workforce still commutes westward toward the Bay Area or south toward Contra Costa County via I-80, a corridor notorious for stop-and-go congestion. At a median home value of $592,500 against a median household income of roughly $102,000, the price-to-income ratio hovers around 5.8 — steep, but meaningfully lower than neighboring Vallejo-to-San Francisco options, which is precisely why the city has grown to over 120,000 residents across nearly 42 square miles of wide, flat Suisun Valley terrain. That valley geography delivers open-sky horizons, golden-brown hills in summer, and an average of 9.5 hours of daily sunshine with comfortable 73°F daytime highs, though winter nights dip to the low 50s with tule fog rolling off the nearby marshlands of Suisun Bay. The city's layout is highway-bisected and car-dependent, with subdivisions spreading outward rather than clustering around a dense walkable core, though the Suisun Valley wine country on the eastern edge and nearby marsh trails offer genuine outdoor texture. Fairfield is essentially a place where Bay Area economics meet Central Valley geography — affordable by regional standards, anchored by federal employment, but stretched thin across enough asphalt that daily life revolves around the car.
